back: An illness that lasts a long time and usually develops slowly, e.g. diabetes, hypertension.
A disease that cannot be passed from one person to another.
A condition in which the body cannot control blood sugar because it makes too little insulin or cannot use it properly.
Blood pressure that stays too high over a long time; a 'silent killer'.
Testing people who feel well to find a disease early, e.g. a blood pressure check.

front: Name four risk factors we can change.
back: Unhealthy diet, physical inactivity, tobacco use, harmful use of alcohol (also overweight, stress).

front: Give two possible complications of uncontrolled diabetes.
back: Blindness, kidney damage, foot wounds and amputation, heart disease or stroke.

front: Give three effects of chronic illness on the nation.
back: Pressure on hospitals, high spending on medicines, loss of skilled workers and productivity.
